facts.material: Composite laminate of PET film and polyethylene film, both plastics
facts.form: Film in sheet or roll form, laminated composite

gri_path: GRI 1: Heading 3920 text expressly covers plastic film 'laminated, supported or similarly combined with other materials,' matching a PET/PE plastic laminate
GRI 6: Subheading 3920.62 covers film of poly(ethylene terephthalate), the identifying/essential-character layer of this laminate

rejected_alternatives.reason: Heading 3921 requires reinforcement with non-plastic materials or cellular structure; this laminate is constructed entirely of plastic layers (PET and PE), which N351059 holds is excluded from 3921 and belongs in 3920

missing_facts: Relative proportion by weight/thickness of PET vs PE, though PET layer is presumed to give essential character per cited rulings and heading text specifying PET subheading
Whether film is metallized or coated with non-plastic material (would change classification)
classification.rationale: Heading 3920 expressly covers noncellular, non-reinforced plastic film 'laminated, supported or similarly combined with other materials,' which is precisely the PET/PE laminate structure described. Chapter 39 note does not exclude such films, and heading 3921 is reserved for films reinforced with non-plastic materials or cellular plastics, neither of which applies here since the laminate is constructed entirely of plastic layers, as confirmed by in-force ruling N351059 and consistent with N338010 and N326371. Because PET is a named subheading (3920.62) and typically the identifying layer in such packaging laminates, the product is classified under 3920.62.00.90 (Other, of PET), pending confirmation of exact layer proportions.

3920.argument: Heading 3920 covers 'Other plates, sheets, film, foil and strip, of plastics, noncellular and not reinforced, laminated, supported or similarly combined with other materials.' The product is a laminated composite film of PET (polyethylene terephthalate) and polyethylene, both plastic materials. The heading text explicitly includes 'laminated' and 'similarly combined with other materials,' which directly describes this composite structure. Subheading 3920.62 specifically covers PET films. Since the product is not metallized and is a general-purpose packaging film, it falls under 3920.62.00.90 (Other). Chapter 39 note 2 does not exclude plastic films from heading 3920. The product is noncellular plastic film not reinforced with non-plastic materials, so it is not excluded to heading 3921. Multiple in-force CROSS rulings (N338010, N351059, N326371) confirm that laminated and composite plastic films composed entirely of plastic layers are classified in heading 3920, not 3921. Ruling N351059 explicitly states that products 'constructed entirely of plastic layers' are excluded from heading 3921 and classified in 3920.
exclusions_against: Chapter 39 note 2(l) excludes synthetic rubber and articles thereof, but this product is plastic film, not rubber
Chapter 39 note 2(p) excludes textiles, but this is plastic film
Heading 3921 (reinforced plastic sheets) is excluded because the product contains only plastic layers, not reinforcement with non-plastic materials

3921.argument: Heading 3921 covers 'Other plates, sheets, film, foil and strip, of plastics' that are reinforced with materials other than plastic or are cellular. The product is a laminated composite of PET (polyethylene terephthalate) and polyethylene film—two different plastic materials bonded together. Under GRI 3(b), composite goods are classified by the material giving them essential character. Both materials are plastics, making this a plastic-to-plastic laminate. The heading text of 3921 explicitly covers 'plates, sheets, film, foil and strip, of plastics' and includes laminated structures. The product qualifies as a laminated plastic film under 3921. The best 10-digit code is 3921.90.40.90 (Other: Flexible: Other), which covers flexible plastic films of other plastics not otherwise specified. The laminated structure and packaging function support classification in 3921 rather than 3920, which is limited to noncellular plastics 'not reinforced, laminated, supported or similarly combined with other materials'—a heading that would exclude multi-layer plastic composites.
exclusions_against: Heading 3920 explicitly states 'noncellular and not reinforced, laminated, supported or similarly combined with other materials,' which excludes laminated plastic-to-plastic composites. Ruling N331595 and N351059 both hold that plastic films laminated to other plastic materials are excluded from 3921 and classified in 3920 instead, directly contradicting the argument for 3921. Ruling N351059 specifically states: 'Heading 3921 covers plates, sheets, film, foil and strip, of plastics that have been reinforced with materials other than plastic. As this product is constructed entirely of plastic layers it is excluded from classification in 3921.90.4090.'

gri_path: GRI 1: Heading 3918 specifically names 'Floor coverings of plastics, whether or not self-adhesive, in rolls or in the form of tiles' which describes PVC vinyl tiles directly
GRI 6: Subheading 3918.10 covers 'Of polymers of vinyl chloride'; within that, 'Floor coverings: Vinyl tile' is the applicable 8-digit line
GRI 6: At the 10-digit level, 'Other' (3918.10.10.40) applies absent a specified rigid solid or rigid expanded polymer core construction

rejected_alternatives.reason: Heading 3918 is more specific for floor coverings in tile form of plastics; 3920 is a residual sheet/plate provision
Heading 3926 is a residual 'other articles of plastics' provision that does not prevail over the specific floor covering provision of 3918

missing_facts: Core structure (rigid solid polymer core, rigid expanded polymer core, or other) which could shift the applicable 10-digit statistical suffix under 3918.10.10
Whether tiles are self-adhesive (affects description but not heading since 3918 covers both)
classification.rationale: Heading 3918 expressly covers floor coverings of plastics in tile form, and PVC vinyl tiles fall squarely within this description under GRI 1, with subheading 3918.10 covering polymers of vinyl chloride and the 'Vinyl tile' line matching exactly. Chapter 39 note 2 contains no exclusion for floor coverings, and Section VII note 2 confirms heading 3918 is the proper home for such plastic articles. Multiple in-force CROSS rulings (N341739, N261168, N327606) confirm PVC vinyl tiles are classified under 3918.10; absent specification of a rigid solid or rigid expanded polymer core construction, the residual 'Other' 10-digit line (3918.10.10.40) is used, though confirming the core structure would allow a more precise statistical suffix.

3918.argument: Heading 3918 covers floor coverings of plastics in the form of tiles. The product is PVC vinyl tile, a plastic floor covering in tile form. Chapter 39 note 1 defines plastics as materials capable of being formed by molding, casting, extruding, rolling or other processes into shapes retained on removal of external influence—PVC meets this definition. Chapter 39 note 2 contains no exclusion that removes floor coverings from chapter 39. Section VII note 2 explicitly carves out an exception for headings 3918 and 3919 regarding printed goods, confirming these headings are intended to cover plastic floor coverings. Subheading 3918.10 applies to floor coverings of polymers of vinyl chloride, which directly matches PVC tiles. The 10-digit code 3918.10.10.40 classifies vinyl tile under the "Other" category, appropriate for standard PVC vinyl tiles not specifically described as rigid solid polymer core or rigid expanded polymer core variants. Multiple in-force CROSS rulings (N341739, N261168, N327606) confirm that PVC vinyl tiles are classified under 3918.10, with specific 10-digit codes depending on core construction. For a standard PVC vinyl tile without specification of core type, 3918.10.10.40 is the appropriate residual provision.

3920.argument: Heading 3920 covers 'Other plates, sheets, film, foil and strip, of plastics, noncellular and not reinforced, laminated, supported or similarly combined with other materials.' PVC vinyl tiles are plastic sheets in tile form made from polyvinyl chloride. Chapter 39 note 2 does not exclude plastic floor coverings from Chapter 39. While heading 3918 specifically covers 'Floor coverings of plastics, whether or not self-adhesive, in rolls or in the form of tiles,' heading 3920 is a residual category for plastic plates and sheets of other plastics not specifically enumerated in earlier headings. Under GRI 3(a), the more specific heading (3918) should be preferred when goods are prima facie classifiable under two headings. Heading 3918 explicitly names floor coverings in tile form, making it more specific than the general category of plastic sheets in heading 3920. The product's essential character and function as a floor covering tile aligns with heading 3918's scope rather than heading 3920's broader category of plastic sheets and strips.
exclusions_against: Chapter 39 note 2(o) excludes wall coverings of heading 4814, but does not exclude floor coverings
Heading 3918 is more specific than heading 3920 for floor coverings in tile form, making 3920 a weaker classification under GRI 3(a)

3926.argument: Heading 3926 covers 'Other articles of plastics' under Chapter 39. PVC vinyl tiles are plastic articles made from polyvinyl chloride, a plastic material defined in Chapter 39 note 1. However, this argument faces a critical obstacle: Heading 3918 specifically and directly covers 'Floor coverings of plastics, whether or not self-adhesive, in rolls or in the form of tiles' with a subheading 3918.10 for 'Of polymers of vinyl chloride.' The product description explicitly identifies the tiles as floor coverings made from PVC. Under GRI 1 (headings and notes), heading 3918 is the more specific provision that directly names floor coverings of plastics in tile form. Heading 3926 is a residual category for 'other articles of plastics' and applies only when goods do not fall within more specific headings. Multiple in-force CROSS rulings (N261168, N327606) consistently classify PVC vinyl tiles under heading 3918.10, not 3926. The argument for 3926 fails because 3918 is more specific and directly applicable.
exclusions_against: Chapter 39 note 2(o) excludes 'Wall coverings of heading 4814' but does not exclude floor coverings, which are covered by heading 3918 instead
Heading 3918 is more specific than heading 3926 under GRI 3(a); floor coverings of plastics in tile form are explicitly named in 3918, making 3926 inapplicable

The product is a floor covering in tile form made of PVC, which directly matches the description of heading 3918.10 ('Floor coverings of plastics...in the form of tiles: Of polymers of vinyl chloride')

facts.material: 50% cotton / 50% polyester blended knit jersey fabric
facts.form: Complete knitted garment with rib knit crew neckline (no front opening), short hemmed sleeves, straight hemmed bottom

gri_path: GRI 1: heading 6109 covers 'T-shirts, singlets, tank tops and similar garments, knitted or crocheted'; the crew-neck pullover construction with no front opening is a T-shirt, not a 'shirt' of heading 6105, which Chapter 61 Note 4 defines as requiring a full or partial front opening starting at the neckline

GRI 1: Chapter 61 Note 4 exclusions for 6105 (drawstring/ribbed waistband tightening) are not at issue since good is classified in 6109, but confirms 6109 is proper heading for pullover-style short-sleeve knit tops

Section XI Note 2(A): fabric is 50% cotton / 50% man-made fiber, an equal blend with no single material predominating by weight; where two or more headings/subheadings each equally merit consideration for part of the material, the good is classified as if consisting wholly of the material corresponding to the heading/subheading that occurs last in numerical order
GRI 6: applying Note 2(A) at the subheading level, subheading 6109.90 (Of other textile materials/man-made fibers) occurs after 6109.10 (Of cotton), so the man-made fiber subheading governs
GRI 6: within 6109.90.10, select statistical suffix for Boys' short-sleeve knit T-shirt
classification.deciding_gri: GRI 6 (with Section XI Note 2(A) resolving the equal-weight blend tie)

rejected_alternatives.reason: Heading 6105 is limited to 'shirts,' which Chapter 61 Note 4 defines as garments with a full or partial front opening at the neckline; a crew-neck pullover T-shirt lacks that opening and is properly a T-shirt of heading 6109, not a shirt of 6105

This line is 'Of cotton,' but the fabric is an equal 50/50 cotton-polyester blend with no material predominating; Section XI Note 2(A) directs classification under the subheading that occurs last in numerical order among those equally meriting consideration, i.e., 6109.90 (man-made fiber), not 6109.10 (cotton)

classification.rationale: The garment is a knit, crew-neck, short-sleeve pullover, which is a T-shirt of heading 6109 rather than a 'shirt' of 6105 because it lacks the front opening Chapter 61 Note 4 requires for shirts. Because the fabric is exactly 50% cotton and 50% polyester with no material predominating by weight, Section XI Note 2(A) requires treating the good as if wholly of the fiber corresponding to the subheading occurring last in numerical order among equally meriting subheadings, which is 6109.90 (man-made fibers) rather than 6109.10 (cotton). Within that line, the statistical suffix for boys' T-shirts is 6109.90.10.09. Confidence is moderate because the fiber-tie rule is dispositive here but depends on confirming no material predominates and that the polyester is genuinely 'man-made fiber' rather than another textile category.

6105.argument: Heading 6105 covers 'Men's or boys' shirts, knitted or crocheted.' The product is a complete, made-up boys' T-shirt of knitted jersey fabric with a crew neckline, short sleeves, and hemmed bottom—all hallmarks of a shirt under Chapter 61. Chapter 61 Note 1 requires that the chapter applies only to 'made up knitted or crocheted articles,' which this product satisfies. Chapter 61 Note 4 defines shirts as 'garments designed to cover the upper part of the body, having long or short sleeves and a full or partial opening starting at the neckline.' This T-shirt meets that definition. The product is 50% cotton and 50% polyester. Under Section XI Note 2(A), when no single textile material predominates by weight, goods are classified as if consisting wholly of the material covered by the heading that occurs last in numerical order among those that equally merit consideration. Between cotton (6105.10) and man-made fibers (6105.20), heading 6105.20 occurs last numerically, making it the proper classification. However, the product can also be classified under 6105.10 (Of cotton) because cotton is one of the two equal components. The best code under 6105.10 for boys' short-sleeved T-shirts is 6105.10.00.30 ('Boys': Other'). The product meets all requirements: it is a knitted shirt, made-up, with short sleeves, a crew neckline, and hemmed construction. No exclusions in Chapter 61 Note 2 or Note 4 apply—the garment has sleeves (Note 4 excludes sleeveless garments from 6105), has no pockets below the waist, and has sufficient stitch density (finely knit jersey).
exclusions_against: Chapter 61 Note 4 excludes from heading 6105 garments with pockets below the waist, a ribbed waistband or other means of tightening at the bottom, or average stitch density less than 10 stitches per linear centimeter. The product description does not indicate any of these exclusionary features, so none apply. Chapter 61 Note 4 also excludes sleeveless garments from 6105; this product has short sleeves, so it is not excluded.

6109.argument: Heading 6109 covers T-shirts, singlets, tank tops and similar garments, knitted or crocheted. The product is a boys' T-shirt made of 50% cotton and 50% polyester blend, finely knit jersey fabric with rib knit crew neckline, short hemmed sleeves, and straight hemmed bottom. Chapter 61 note 1 requires that the chapter applies only to made up knitted or crocheted articles—this product qualifies. Chapter 61 note 5 excludes garments with drawstring, ribbed waistband or other means of tightening at the bottom; this product has a straight hemmed bottom, so it is not excluded. Section XI note 2(A) provides that goods of mixed textile materials are classified as if consisting wholly of the material which predominates by weight. Since cotton and polyester are equal at 50% each, the rule directs classification under the heading which occurs last in numerical order among those which equally merit consideration. However, the product contains cotton, making 6109.10 (Of cotton) the appropriate subheading. Under GRI 6, the 10-digit code 6109.10.00.14 applies to boys' T-shirts, other, other T-shirts, boys', which matches the product description.
exclusions_against: Chapter 61 note 5 excludes garments with drawstring, ribbed waistband or other means of tightening at the bottom—this product has a straight hemmed bottom, so the exclusion does not apply

facts.material: Metal and plastic components (valve, housing, tubing, regulator)
facts.function: Dispenses bottled beer via hand-operated valve using compressed CO2 pressure

gri_path: GRI 1: Heading 8210 expressly covers 'hand-operated mechanical appliances, weighing 10 kg or less, used in the preparation, conditioning or serving of food or drink'
Chapter 82 Note 1 exception explicitly excepts heading 8210 goods from the working-edge/blade requirement, so a hand-operated valve appliance for serving beverages qualifies
GRI 1 rejects 8481 because that heading covers valves/taps as standalone fittings for pipes/tanks, not a complete hand-operated serving appliance more specifically described by 8210
GRI 3(a): 8210 is the more specific heading for a complete hand-operated food/drink serving appliance versus the general valve provision of 8481 or residual machinery provision of 8479

rejected_alternatives.reason: 8481 covers standalone valves/taps for pipes and tanks; the product is a complete hand-operated serving appliance more specifically described by 8210, and R01157 held a similar drink dispenser belongs in 8210 rather than a valve heading
Chapter 39 note 2(s) excludes articles of Section XVI/mechanical appliances; the product's essential character is a mechanical serving appliance, not simple plastic tableware
8479 is residual for machines not elsewhere specified; heading 8210 more specifically names hand-operated appliances for serving food or drink weighing 10 kg or less

missing_facts: Confirm actual weight of the assembled unit does not exceed 10 kg, which is required for heading 8210
classification.rationale: Heading 8210 specifically and completely describes a hand-operated mechanical appliance weighing 10 kg or less used in serving food or drink, which matches this hand-operated beer dispenser exactly; Chapter 82 Note 1 explicitly excepts heading 8210 from the blade/working-part requirement, removing the main objection to classifying it in Chapter 82. In-force ruling R01157 classified an analogous hand-operated drink dispenser with valves under 8210.00.0000 rather than under 8481, supporting this outcome under GRI 1/GRI 3(a) as the more specific heading for a complete serving appliance. The valve heading 8481 and residual machinery heading 8479 are rejected because they describe components or generic machines, not the complete hand-operated serving appliance named in 8210. Confidence is tempered pending confirmation that the unit's weight is at or under the 10 kg statutory limit.

8481.argument: Heading 8481 covers 'Taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances, for pipes, boiler shells, tanks, vats or the like, including pressure-reducing valves and thermostatically controlled valves; parts thereof.' A home beer dispenser with a hand-operated valve and compressed CO2 regulator is a valve appliance that controls the flow of pressurized gas and liquid. The product functions as a tap or valve mechanism—it has a hand-operated valve that regulates flow using compressed CO2 pressure, a regulator to control gas pressure, and tubing to deliver beer. The Harmonized System Explanatory Notes to heading 84.81 state that this heading covers 'taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances' used to control the flow of fluids and gases. The product is not a pump (8414), not a hand tool (8205), and not a domestic appliance under 8509 because it is fundamentally a valve-based control device, not an electromechanical appliance. Under GRI 6, subheading 8481.80 covers 'Other appliances' (beyond pressure-reducing and check valves), and 8481.80.50 is the appropriate line for hand-operated valve appliances of materials other than copper or iron/steel (the product contains plastic and metal components). The ruling H250151 (Coravin wine tap system, in force) classified a similar hand-operated pressurized beverage dispensing device with a valve and gas regulator in heading 8481.80.50, establishing direct precedent. The ruling H85470 (carbonators for beverage systems, in force) classified beverage system appliances with CO2 regulators and control mechanisms in heading 8481.80.90.
exclusions_against: Chapter 84 note 1(f) excludes 'Electromechanical domestic appliances of heading 8509,' but this product is not electromechanical—it is hand-operated and mechanical only, so the exclusion does not apply.
Section XVI note 1 excludes articles of chapters 82, 83, 90, 91, and 95, but a valve appliance is not a hand tool (82), base metal article (83), optical instrument (90), clock (91), or toy (95).

8210.argument: Heading 8210 covers 'Hand-operated mechanical appliances, weighing 10 kg or less, used in the preparation, conditioning or serving of food or drink, and base metal parts thereof.' The home beer dispenser is a hand-operated mechanical appliance (activated by a hand-operated valve) designed specifically for serving beverages (beer). It weighs 10 kg or less and consists of metal and plastic components. The product fits squarely within the statutory language of heading 8210. Chapter 82 Note 1(a) requires articles to have 'a blade, working edge, working surface or other working part' of base metal, but heading 8210 is explicitly carved out from this requirement ('Apart from...goods of heading 8209, this chapter covers only...'). The hand-operated valve mechanism that controls the flow of beer using compressed CO2 constitutes the working part. The primary function—serving beverages—matches the heading's express scope. Ruling R01157 (in force, 2004) classified a 4-shot drink dispenser with a hand-operated butterfly handle and valves under 8210.00.0000, finding it 'more specifically provided for in Chapter 82' than in heading 7323 (household articles). That ruling directly supports classification of this beer dispenser under 8210.
exclusions_against: Chapter 82 Note 1(a) excludes most articles unless they have a blade, working edge, working surface or other working part of base metal—but heading 8210 is explicitly excepted from this restriction by the phrase 'Apart from...goods of heading 8209'

Section XVI Note 1(k) excludes 'Articles of chapter 82' from Section XVI (machinery), which confirms that hand-operated mechanical appliances for food/drink service belong in Chapter 82, not in machinery headings like 8481 (valves) or 8414 (pumps)

3924.argument: Heading 3924 covers 'Tableware, kitchenware, other household articles and hygienic or toilet articles, of plastics.' A home beer dispenser with metal and plastic components (valve, housing, tubing, regulator) designed to dispense bottled beer using hand-operated valve and compressed CO2 is a household article of plastics used for beverage service. The product is a complete assembled home appliance for serving beverages, falling within the scope of 'other household articles' under 3924. The plastic housing and components constitute the essential material. Subheading 3924.90.56.50 ('Other') is the appropriate 10-digit code for household articles of plastics not specifically enumerated elsewhere in heading 3924. Recent CROSS rulings N341069 (2025) and N353515 (2025) classify plastic beverage dispensers with hand-operated spigots as 3924.10.4000 (tableware and kitchenware, other), establishing precedent that plastic beverage dispensers for home use belong in heading 3924.
exclusions_against: Chapter 39 note 2(s) excludes 'Articles of section XVI (machines and mechanical or electrical appliances)' — a beer dispenser with integrated valve and regulator mechanism could be argued to be a mechanical appliance under Chapter 84 (heading 8481, taps and valves) or Chapter 82 (heading 8210, hand-operated mechanical appliances for food/drink service), as suggested by ruling R01157 (in force, classifying a drink dispenser at 8210.00.0000) and the revoked ruling N016275 which initially classified a liquor dispenser at 8481.80.5090 before being revoked and reclassified to 3926.90.98 by H044956.

8479.argument: A home beer dispenser designed to dispense bottled beer using a hand-operated valve and compressed CO2 is a machine and mechanical appliance having an individual function not specified or included elsewhere in Chapter 84. Heading 8479 is the residual provision for machines with individual functions not covered by more specific headings (8401–8424, 8486). The product is a complete, assembled mechanical appliance that controls beverage flow through a hand-operated valve and pressure regulator using compressed gas. While it incorporates valve components, the essential character is that of a complete dispensing machine, not merely a valve component. The product does not fall under heading 8481 (taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances) because it is an integrated machine system designed to perform the complete function of dispensing, not a standalone valve or tap. Rulings H250151 (Coravin wine dispenser) and H317696 (beverage dispenser machines) both address similar pressurized beverage dispensing devices; H250151 classified a handheld pressurized wine dispenser under 8481 (valves), but that device was a handheld tool primarily functioning as a valve mechanism. H317696 involved large commercial beverage dispensers with solenoid valves and was classified under 8481.80.90. The instant product is a home appliance—a complete, self-contained machine designed to dispense beer, making it more akin to the residual machinery provision of 8479.89.95 than to the valve-specific provisions of 8481. Code 8479.89.95.00 is the appropriate 10-digit statistical line for other machines and mechanical appliances not elsewhere specified.
exclusions_against: Chapter 84 Note 1(f) excludes electromechanical domestic appliances of heading 8509, but a beer dispenser is not an electromechanical domestic appliance in the sense of that exclusion (which covers vacuum cleaners, washing machines, etc.); it is a mechanical appliance without electrical actuation of the dispensing function.

Heading 8481 (Taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances) is more specific for valve components, but the product is an integrated machine system, not a valve offered for installation in pipes or tanks. The essential character is the complete dispensing machine, not the valve component within it.

classification.rationale: Heading 6110 clearly covers the knitted sweater under GRI 1 and Chapter 61 Note 1. Because the garment blends cotton, nylon, and metallic yarn, Section XI Note 2 requires classification by predominant textile material weight; absent contrary fiber-content data, the man-made fiber (nylon) plus metalized yarn treatment supports 6110.30 as argued by the memo and supported by in-force rulings K85028 and N341057 on comparable mixed-fiber women's sweaters. The 'Other' residual subheading 6110.30.30 applies since no special wool/silk/leather content is indicated, with the women's statistical suffix .20 selected per the garment's stated end use.confidence lowered slightly because exact fiber percentages were not provided, which could shift the classification to 6110.20 (cotton) if cotton predominates.

6110.argument: Heading 6110 covers sweaters, pullovers, sweatshirts and similar articles, knitted or crocheted. The product is a complete, finished women's knitted sweater made from a blend of cotton, nylon (man-made fiber), and metallic yarn. Chapter 61 Note 1 requires that the chapter applies only to made up knitted or crocheted articles, which this sweater satisfies. Section XI Note 2(A) and (B) govern classification of goods of mixed textile materials: goods are classified as if consisting wholly of the textile material which predominates by weight, or if no single material predominates, by the heading which occurs last in numerical order. The product contains cotton, nylon, and metallic yarn in a blend. Under Section XI Note 2(B)(a), metalized yarn (heading 5605) is treated as a single textile material. The blend does not appear to be predominantly cotton or wool. Since the product is a blend of multiple fibers including man-made fibers (nylon) and metallic yarn, it falls under 6110.30 (Of man-made fibers). Within 6110.30, the product does not contain 25% or more leather, 23% or more wool/fine animal hair, or 30% or more silk/silk waste, so it classifies under 6110.30.30 (Other), which further subdivides to 6110.30.3020 for women's or girls' sweaters. This classification is supported by in-force rulings K85028 and N341057, which classified women's knitted sweaters with mixed fiber compositions including cotton, nylon, and metallic yarn under 6110.30.3020.
exclusions_against: Chapter 61 Note 2(a) excludes goods of heading 6212 (not applicable—this is a sweater, not a special garment)
Chapter 61 Note 2(b) excludes worn clothing or articles of heading 6309 (not applicable—product is new)
Chapter 61 Note 2(c) excludes orthopedic appliances and surgical items (not applicable—this is a fashion sweater)

Same Section XVI note 2(e) exclusion applies regardless of spark-ignition vs compression-ignition distinction
Heading 8413 covers pumps for liquids and fuel pumps for engines; a pressure regulator is not a pump and does not move fuel, it controls pressure/flow of gas

missing_facts: Whether the regulator is a standalone valve or is integrated into a complete fuel system/tank assembly (which could shift classification toward 8708 for a complete vehicle fuel system)
Whether the regulator is hydraulic fluid power type or a filter-regulator (would change 8-digit line)
classification.rationale: The product is described generically as 'a fuel regulator for gaseous-fueled engines,' which functions as a pressure-reducing valve for gas — a device named explicitly in heading 8481. Section XVI Note 2(e) excludes articles of heading 8481 from being treated as parts of engines (heading 8409) unless they are integral parts of the engine itself, which is not established here for a standalone regulator. Absent evidence that this regulator is part of an integrated motor vehicle fuel-tank system (as in H262289), the standalone pressure-reducing valve function controls under GRI 1, landing in 8481.10.00.90 as it is not the hydraulic-fluid-power or filter-regulator type.

8481.argument: A fuel regulator for gaseous-fueled engines is a valve-type appliance that regulates fuel pressure and flow. Heading 8481 covers 'Taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances, for pipes, boiler shells, tanks, vats or the like, including pressure-reducing valves and thermostatically controlled valves; parts thereof.' The fuel regulator functions as a pressure-reducing valve, which is explicitly named in the heading. The Explanatory Notes to heading 8481 confirm that the heading covers devices designed to regulate the pressure or flow velocity of a gas, operated by automatic devices such as pressure capsules. A fuel regulator for gaseous engines (natural gas or LP gas) reduces high-pressure gas from the fuel tank to usable engine pressure, fitting squarely within this description. Section XVI note 2 and Section XVII note 2 do not exclude heading 8481 from application to fuel system components. While ruling H262289 classified an integrated CNG fuel tank system as a motor vehicle part (8708.99.8180) because the entire system was specially designed for trucks, a standalone fuel regulator is not a complete fuel tank system and is not excluded by Section XVII note 2(e), which only excludes articles of heading 8481 when they constitute integral parts of engines or motors. The regulator is a separate appliance suitable for use with gaseous-fueled engines generally. Subheading 8481.10.00 covers pressure-reducing valves. The best 10-digit code is 8481.10.00.90 (Other pressure-reducing valves), as the regulator does not fall within the more specific subcategories of hydraulic fluid power type (8481.10.00.20) or filter-regulators (8481.10.00.40).
exclusions_against: Section XVII note 2(e) excludes 'articles of heading 8481 or 8482 or, provided they constitute integral parts of engines or motors, articles of heading 8483' from the definition of motor vehicle parts. However, this exclusion applies only when the valve constitutes an integral part of an engine or motor itself, not when it is a separate fuel system component.

8409.argument: A fuel regulator for gaseous-fueled engines is a part suitable for use solely or principally with internal combustion engines of heading 8407 or 8408. Heading 8409 covers 'Parts suitable for use solely or principally with the engines of heading 8407 or 8408.' The fuel regulator regulates fuel pressure and flow, making it an essential component part of the fuel delivery system for gaseous-fueled (natural gas or LP gas) internal combustion engines. Since the product is designed for gaseous-fueled engines (not spark-ignition gasoline engines), it falls under 8409.99 (Other parts for compression-ignition or other engines) rather than 8409.91 (spark-ignition engines). The most specific 10-digit code is 8409.99.99.90 (Other), which covers miscellaneous engine parts not otherwise specified. Section XVI note 2(b) confirms that parts suitable for use solely or principally with a particular kind of machine are classified with that machine or in heading 8409 as appropriate. Chapter 84 note 1 does not exclude engine parts from chapter 84 coverage.
exclusions_against: Section XVI note 2(e) excludes articles of heading 8481 (valves and pressure-reducing appliances) when they are not integral parts of engines or motors. However, a fuel regulator integrated into an engine fuel system and suitable solely for use with gaseous engines qualifies as an integral part and engine component, not a standalone valve appliance.

H262289 classified a CNG fuel tank system (including high-pressure regulator) under 8708.99.8180 (motor vehicle parts), but that ruling involved a complete integrated tank system for vehicles. A standalone fuel regulator component for gaseous engines is more appropriately classified as an engine part under 8409 rather than as a vehicle accessory under 8708.

8407.argument: Heading 8407 covers spark-ignition reciprocating or rotary internal combustion piston engines. A fuel regulator for gaseous-fueled engines is a part suitable for use solely or principally with such engines. Under Section XVI Note 2(b) and Chapter 84 Note 2, parts of engines classified in heading 8407 or 8408 that are suitable for use solely or principally with those engines are classified in heading 8409 (Parts suitable for use solely or principally with the engines of heading 8407 or 8408). The fuel regulator regulates fuel pressure and flow for gaseous-fueled internal combustion engines, making it a component integral to engine operation. Ruling G85192 (2000) established that various parts for gasoline engines (oil fill tube, fuel tank, blower housing) are classified under 8409.91.9990 as parts suitable for use solely or principally with spark-ignition engines. Ruling N343403 (2024) confirms that engine parts (pistons, connecting rods, rings) for spark-ignition engines are classified under 8409.91 subheadings. The fuel regulator, being a complete assembly designed specifically to regulate fuel delivery to gaseous-fueled spark-ignition engines, falls within the scope of heading 8409 as a part suitable for use solely or principally with such engines. The best 10-digit code is 8409.91.5085 (Other parts for spark-ignition engines, other).
exclusions_against: Section XVI Note 2(e) excludes articles of heading 8481 (valves and pressure-reducing appliances) when they constitute integral parts of engines or motors, but a standalone fuel regulator for gaseous-fueled engines is classified as an engine part under 8409, not as a valve under 8481

8413.argument: Heading 8413 covers 'Pumps for liquids, whether or not fitted with a measuring device; liquid elevators; parts thereof.' Subheading 8413.30 specifically addresses 'Fuel, lubricating or cooling medium pumps for internal combustion piston engines.' A fuel regulator for gaseous-fueled engines functions as a pressure-control device within the fuel delivery system for internal combustion engines. While the product's primary function is regulation rather than pumping, the CROSS ruling N249681 (in_force) classifies fuel delivery system components for internal combustion engines under 8413.30.90.30 (fuel pumps). The regulator is an integral part of the fuel delivery system for gaseous-fueled piston engines and falls within the scope of heading 8413 as a component suitable for use solely or principally with such engines. The best available 10-digit code is 8413.30.90.90 (Other), as the product does not fit the more specific 'fuel pumps' category (8413.30.90.30) but remains classifiable under the broader 'other' provision for fuel, lubricating or cooling medium pumps for internal combustion piston engines.
exclusions_against: Heading 8481 (Taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances, including pressure-reducing valves) presents a competing classification. The CROSS ruling H224997 (in_force) indicates that fuel flow regulators designed to regulate pressure or flow velocity may be classified under 8481 as control valves. However, when a component is part of an integrated fuel delivery system for internal combustion engines and is suitable for use solely or principally with such engines, Section XVI note 2(b) directs classification with the machines of that kind (heading 8413) rather than as a standalone valve (heading 8481).

facts.function: Controls fluid flow and pressure within an automatic transmission hydraulic control valve assembly
facts.form: Discrete spool valve part/component, not a complete valve body
facts.end_use: Installed in automatic transmissions of motor vehicles to regulate hydraulic fluid flow

gri_path: GRI 1: Heading 8481 covers 'taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances ... including pressure-reducing valves and thermostatically controlled valves; parts thereof' — the spool valve is a part of a valve controlling hydraulic fluid

Section XVI Note 2(b): parts suitable solely or principally for use with a particular kind of machine are classified with that machine's parts heading; a valve part is classified under 8481.90 rather than under the transmission's own heading (8708/8483) because 8481 is the specific provision for valves and their parts
GRI 6: Within 8481.90 (Parts), the item is not a 'valve body' (8481.90.90.20/.60) but a smaller internal component (the spool), so it falls to the residual 'Other' line 8481.90.90.40

rejected_alternatives.reason: General motor-vehicle-parts provision yields to the more specific valve/parts heading 8481 per Additional U.S. Rule 1(c)
Heading 8483 covers transmission shafts/gears/gearboxes, not hydraulic control valve components
Those lines are specifically for 'valve bodies,' whereas a spool is an internal moving element, not the body itself

missing_facts: Whether the spool is a complete valve body or only an internal sliding element
Exact metal composition, which could affect the statistical suffix
classification.rationale: The spool valve part functions as a component of a valve controlling hydraulic fluid in the transmission, so heading 8481 (valves and parts thereof) is the specific and controlling provision under GRI 1, with Section XVI Note 2(b) directing valve parts to the valve heading rather than to the general motor-vehicle-parts heading 8708 or the transmission-machinery heading 8483. Because the description indicates a 'spool' component rather than a full valve body, it falls to the residual 'Other' statistical line 8481.90.90.40. In-force ruling N348390 supports classifying transmission valve components under 8481.

8708.argument: A transmission spool valve part is a component of an automatic transmission's hydraulic control system. Heading 8708 covers 'Parts and accessories of the motor vehicles of headings 8701 to 8705.' The spool valve is a part of the transmission power train system. Section XVII note 2(e) excludes 'Machines or apparatus of headings 8401 to 8479' from the definition of 'parts and accessories,' but transmission control valves are integral transmission components, not separate machines. The product is not a complete valve assembly (which might fall under 8481) but rather a component part of the transmission itself. Under GRI 1, heading 8708 applies as the specific provision for motor vehicle parts. GRI 6 subheading analysis: 8708.40 covers gearboxes and parts thereof, but a spool valve is not a gearbox part. 8708.99 covers 'Other parts and accessories.' Within 8708.99, the line 8708.99.68 provides for 'Other parts for power trains,' which is the most specific description for a transmission control component. The final 10-digit code 8708.99.68.90 ('Other') is appropriate as the spool valve does not fit the more specific categories (drive shafts, forged universal joints).
exclusions_against: Section XVII note 2(e) excludes machines or apparatus of headings 8401 to 8479, but transmission control valves are integral parts of the transmission, not separate machines or apparatus.
Section XVII note 2(b) excludes parts of general use of base metal, but a spool valve is specifically designed for transmission control and is not a general-use part.

8481.argument: Heading 8481 covers 'Taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances, for pipes, boiler shells, tanks, vats or the like, including pressure-reducing valves and thermostatically controlled valves; parts thereof.' A transmission spool valve part is a component of a valve assembly used in automatic transmission hydraulic systems to control fluid flow and pressure. Section XVI note 2(b) provides that parts suitable for use solely or principally with a particular kind of machine are classified with those machines or in the appropriate parts heading. Subheading 8481.90 covers 'Parts' of valves and similar appliances. The spool valve part, being a component of a transmission control valve assembly, falls within 8481.90. Since it is not a valve body (which would be 8481.90.9020 or 8481.90.9040 for parts of 8481.20 valves), and assuming it is not made of copper, iron, or steel as a complete part, the residual provision 8481.90.90.40 'Other' applies. The product is metal and used in a hydraulic transmission system, making heading 8481 the appropriate classification.
exclusions_against: Section XVI note 1(c) excludes 'Bobbins, spools, cops, cones, cores, reels or similar supports' but this exclusion applies to structural supports, not to spool valve components that function as control elements in a hydraulic system.

8483.argument: Heading 8483 covers transmission shafts, gears, gear boxes, speed changers and parts thereof. A transmission spool valve part is a component of an automatic transmission control system. While the product controls hydraulic fluid flow (a valve function), it is specifically designed as a part of a transmission assembly and functions as an integral component of the transmission's control mechanism. Section XVI note 2(b) provides that parts suitable for use solely or principally with a particular kind of machine are classified with those machines. A spool valve part designed specifically for automatic transmissions would fall under 8483.90 (parts of heading 8483) as a part of the transmission system. The best 10-digit code is 8483.90.80.00 (Other parts, not elsewhere specified).
exclusions_against: Heading 8481 (Taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances) is more specific for valve components. Recent CROSS rulings N348390 (2025) and N268111 (2015) classify transmission valve bodies and valve body assemblies containing spool valves under heading 8481 (specifically 8481.20.0050 for valve assemblies and 8481.90.9020 for valve body parts), not under 8483. Subheading Note 3 to Chapter 84 defines 'valves for oleohydraulic or pneumatic transmissions' as valves used specifically in fluid power transmission, and 8481.20 takes precedence over all other subheadings of heading 8481.

missing_facts: Whether sheets are rectangular (including square) or irregular shape
Specific alloy type (high-strength heat-treatable, heat-treatable industrial, or other) to confirm statistical suffix
Exact thickness to confirm within 6.3 mm or less bracket
classification.rationale: Heading 7606 covers aluminum plates, sheets and strip exceeding 0.2 mm thickness, and the described alloyed, cut-length, not-clad sheets fit squarely within this heading under GRI 1, with no Section XV or Chapter 76 exclusion applying. GRI 6 places the goods under 7606.12 (alloys, not 7606.11 non-alloyed) and then under the not-clad, thickness ≤6.3mm rectangular subheading. Absent specific alloy composition data needed to invoke the high-strength or heat-treatable industrial statistical notes, the residual 'Other' line 7606.12.30.35 is the best-supported statistical suffix, consistent with in-force rulings N301187 and N333593 on similar aluminum alloy sheet products.

7606.argument: Heading 7606 covers aluminum plates, sheets and strip of a thickness exceeding 0.2 mm. The product is alloyed aluminum sheets in cut lengths with various thicknesses exceeding 0.2 mm, matching the heading's scope. Chapter 76 Subheading Note 1(b) defines aluminum alloys as metallic substances in which aluminum predominates by weight over each of the other elements. The product meets this definition. The sheets are not clad (per the facts provided). Under GRI 6, subheading 7606.12 applies to aluminum alloys (as opposed to 7606.11 for non-alloyed aluminum). The 8-digit line 7606.12.30 covers non-clad sheets. The 10-digit code 7606.12.30.35 is the residual 'Other' category for rectangular sheets of aluminum alloys, not clad, with thickness of 6.3 mm or less, that do not fall under the specific high-strength heat-treatable alloys (7606.12.30.15) or heat-treatable industrial alloys (7606.12.30.25) categories, nor the can stock provisions. Section XV note 1 does not exclude aluminum sheets from chapter 76. The product is a raw material for industrial/manufacturing applications, not a finished article or component of machinery, so no exclusions apply.

facts.function: Outerwear jacket for upper body coverage
facts.end_use: Worn by men and boys as casual or athletic outerwear

gri_path: GRI 1: Heading 6101 specifically names anoraks, windbreakers and similar articles, knitted or crocheted, which covers knit jackets
Chapter 61 Note 1 confirms coverage of made-up knitted articles; Note 2 exclusions (worn clothing, orthopedic appliances, 6212) do not apply
GRI 6: subheading 6101.30 for man-made fibers, then 'Other' at 6101.30.20, then statistical suffix 6101.30.20.10 for men's

rejected_alternatives.reason: Heading 6103 covers suit-type jackets and trousers, not outerwear anoraks/jackets like this garment; jacket described lacks suit-coat construction and is not a trouser provision
Heading 6110 covers sweaters/pullovers/similar knit tops, not outerwear jackets with protective/weather function; 6101 is more specific for anoraks/windbreakers/jackets

missing_facts: Whether garment is for men's or boys' sizing specifically (affects statistical suffix 6101.30.20.10 vs .20)
classification.rationale: Heading 6101 expressly names 'anoraks (including ski-jackets), windbreakers and similar articles, knitted or crocheted,' which squarely describes a knit polyester jacket for men and boys; Chapter 61 Note 1 and Note 2 do not exclude it. GRI 1 resolves the heading directly on the heading text and notes. At GRI 6, the man-made fiber subheading 6101.30, 'Other' at 6101.30.20, and the men's statistical suffix 6101.30.20.10 apply, consistent with in-force rulings N283232 and N096117 classifying comparable knit polyester jackets. The competing 6103 and 6110 headings are less specific since the jacket is neither a suit-type coat nor a sweater/pullover-type garment; 6101's explicit reference to anoraks/windbreakers/similar jackets makes it the most specific description under GRI 3(a) reasoning even though GRI 1 alone suffices.

6101.argument: Heading 6101 covers men's or boys' overcoats, carcoats, capes, cloaks, anoraks (including ski-jackets), windbreakers and similar articles, knitted or crocheted. The product is a men's and boys' knit jacket made from 100% polyester, which is a man-made fiber. Chapter 61 Note 1 confirms this chapter applies only to made-up knitted or crocheted articles, which this product satisfies. The product is not excluded by Chapter 61 Note 2 (which excludes goods of heading 6212, worn clothing, and orthopedic appliances). Section XI Note 1 does not exclude textile articles made from man-made fibers. The product falls squarely within the heading text as a knitted jacket for men and boys. Under GRI 6, the subheading 6101.30 applies because the jacket is made of man-made fibers (polyester). The further subdivision 6101.30.20 applies as the jacket does not contain 25% or more leather or 23% or more wool/fine animal hair. The final 10-digit code 6101.30.20.10 applies for men's garments and 6101.30.20.20 for boys' garments. Since the product description states 'mens and boys knit jackets,' the best single code is 6101.30.20.10 for men's, though boys' versions would be classified at 6101.30.20.20.

6103.argument: Heading 6103 covers 'Men's or boys' suits, ensembles, suit-type jackets, blazers, trousers, bib and brace overalls, breeches and shorts (other than swimwear), knitted or crocheted.' The product is a men's and boys' knit jacket made from 100% polyester (synthetic fiber). Chapter 61 Note 1 confirms this chapter applies only to made-up knitted or crocheted articles, which this product is. The jacket qualifies as a 'suit-type jacket' or similar article under heading 6103. At the 6-digit level, 6103.43 covers trousers and similar items of synthetic fibers under heading 6103. The best 10-digit code is 6103.43.15.00, which provides for 'Other' synthetic fiber items under the trousers category, as the product is a knit jacket of synthetic fibers. The material is 100% polyester, a man-made/synthetic fiber, placing it squarely within the synthetic fiber provisions of heading 6103.
exclusions_against: Chapter 61 Note 2(b) excludes worn clothing and articles of heading 6309, which does not apply to new merchandise
Chapter 61 Note 2(c) excludes orthopedic appliances and surgical items, which does not apply to a standard jacket

6110.argument: Heading 6110 covers 'Sweaters, pullovers, sweatshirts, waistcoats (vests) and similar articles, knitted or crocheted.' The product is a men's and boys' knit jacket made from 100% polyester. Chapter 61 note 1 requires that the chapter applies only to made-up knitted or crocheted articles, which this product satisfies. The product is knitted outerwear for the upper body. Under GRI 1, heading 6110 is the appropriate heading as it explicitly covers similar articles (knitted jackets fall within 'similar articles' to sweaters and pullovers). The subheading 6110.30 applies because the garment is made of man-made fibers (100% polyester). The 10-digit code 6110.30.3053 is the most specific provision for men's or boys' knit garments of man-made fibers that are not sweaters, pullovers, sweatshirts, or vests—i.e., 'Other' categories at the 8-digit and 10-digit levels. This classification is supported by ruling N291074 (2017), which classified a 100% polyester men's knit jacket (Style 43233) under 6101.30.2010 as an outerwear jacket, but also classified 100% polyester men's pullover and cardigan garments under 6110.30.3053 when they lacked the character of outerwear. For a standard knit jacket with typical construction features (zipper, collar, sleeves), if it has sufficient protective character for weather, 6101.30.2010 would apply; if it is more of a casual layer piece, 6110.30.3053 applies. Given the product description states 'casual or athletic outerwear,' the stronger case under heading 6110 is 6110.30.3053 as the catch-all for similar knit articles of man-made fibers.
exclusions_against: Chapter 61 note 2(b) excludes worn clothing and articles of heading 6309, which does not apply to new merchandise.
Chapter 61 note 2(c) excludes orthopedic appliances and surgical items, which does not apply.
Section XI note 1 excludes various materials and articles not relevant to a polyester knit garment.
